label: proof
statement: Let a(n,j) be the probability that the strictly descending chain with transitions q(n,j)=1/((n-j)H_(n-1)), 1<=j<n, visits j, where H_k=sum_(r=1)^k 1/r. Put a(j)=6H_(j-1)/(pi^2(j-1)) and g(j)=j when j=2^r for some r>=1, zero otherwise. For every fixed integer L>=0, along n=2^K+L+1 the ratio [sum_(j=2)^(n-L-1) a(n,j)g(j)]/[sum_(j=2)^n a(j)g(j)] tends to infinity. The same holds with the denominator stopped at n-L-1. Thus deleting any fixed-width near-root band does not repair the divergent-series occupation ansatz for polynomially bounded weights.

label: proof
statement: Suppose b_n(j)>=0, b_n(j)=0 for j>n, and b_n(j)->b(j) for every fixed positive integer j. Let f(j)>=0 be finite and S=sum_(j>=1)b(j)f(j)<infinity. Then sum_j b_n(j)f(j)->S if and only if lim_(M->infinity) limsup_(n->infinity) sum_(j>M)b_n(j)f(j)=0. This criterion requires an actual weighted tail estimate; pointwise convergence alone does not supply it.

label: source-backed scope audit
statement: The campaign archived on 7-8 September 2026 refutes both clauses of Aldous-Janson Ansatz 20 using powers-of-two weights and a(n,n)=1. This is a partial answer to P0341: it refutes the unrestricted auxiliary ansatz while leaving general quantitative occupation error bounds and regular-weight repairs unresolved. A ranking label candidate_pa does not mean that no substantive prior result exists. This row records archival scope and claims no new priority.

label: numerical evidence
statement: Numerical evidence only: for twelve seeded real symmetric S3-equivariant kernel pairs with spectra in [0.1,0.9], the optimal expected normalized Hamming coupling distance divided by trace|Q-Qprime|/6 had maximum 0.6934876897518668, with no violation found. The 4096-variable transport LP was checked against DPP normalization, one-site marginals, equivariance, primal residuals and dual objectives; a .3I/.7I commuting control gave ratio 1. Finite-group averaging makes the unrestricted LP optimum an invariant coupling optimum. These finite observations do not prove the general linear bound.

label: proof
statement: For unit vectors v,w in C^n, let P=vv* and Q=ww*. Their determinantal laws are single-site laws with probabilities |v_i|^2 and |w_i|^2. The optimal coupling cost for normalized Hamming distance on subsets of {1,...,n} equals (1/n)sum_i ||v_i|^2-|w_i|^2| and is at most trace|P-Q|/n. If both laws are invariant under a finite permutation group, averaging yields an invariant coupling of the same cost. This is a finite rank-one result, with no general equivariant approximation theorem asserted.

label: proof
statement: Let D be a bounded triangle invariant under reflection R across an axis, and let lambda_1 be the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of -Delta/2 on D. For starting points x and Rx with x off the axis, there is a coalescent coupling of reflected Brownian motions with generator Delta/2 whose meeting time T satisfies P(T>t)<=C_(x,gamma) exp(-gamma t) for every 0<gamma<lambda_1. The coupling reflects one path across the axis until it hits that axis, then uses the same path. The killed half-domain principal eigenvalue is at least lambda_1 by odd extension and the Neumann Rayleigh principle. In particular, the result covers mirror starting pairs in reflection-symmetric acute triangles, not arbitrary pairs or scalene triangles.

label: proof
statement: Let X have a probability law on R with mean m and finite variance sigma^2, and let mu_t be its free convolution with a semicircle law of variance t. For every t>0 with t>=1024(7+4sqrt(2))sigma^2, the continuous density of mu_t has a unique global maximizer M(t), and M(t)->m as t tends to infinity. If M3=E|X-m|^3 is finite, put B=(sqrt(2)+2)sigma, A=B^2+sigma^2 and K=A(B+sigma)+4(B^3+M3); then |M(t)-m|<=36K/t at those times. For sigma=0 the mode is exactly m. These are sufficient large-time bounds for a global density maximizer, without a compact-support assumption or a claimed optimal transition threshold.

label: proof
statement: Let X have a probability law on R with E|X|^7<infinity, mean m, and central moments mu_k=E[(X-m)^k]. Normalize free Brownian motion as convolution with a semicircle law of variance t. Its unique sufficiently-large-time global density maximizer obeys m-3mu_3/t+(5mu_5-22mu_2mu_3)/t^2+O_mu(t^-3). With epsilon=1/t, the equations E[1/(r+epsilon(u-X)^2)]=1 and E[(u-X)/(r+epsilon(u-X)^2)^2]=0 have a C^3 branch at the limiting point (epsilon,u,r)=(0,m,1); finite seventh moment justifies one-sided derivatives and a C^3 extension in epsilon, and the global-mode lemma identifies the branch. An exponential quadratic moment implies this hypothesis. The remainder is law dependent and no originality certificate is asserted.

label: source-backed scope correction
statement: Source correction: Biskup arXiv:1712.09972v4, Theorem 12.19, equation (12.86), and Problem 16.4 concern the joint density rho^D(x,t) in maximizer position x and centered maximum height t. At fixed t its measure in position is A -> exp(-alpha t) E[Z^D(A)exp(-alpha^-1 exp(-alpha t)Z^D(D))]. Integrating over t gives the related marginal E[Z^D(A)/Z^D(D)] when the total mass is almost surely finite and positive. A marginal-only intake statement narrows the primary target; neither explicit joint nor marginal density is resolved by this correction.

label: proof; Lean unavailable
statement: Let Z be a random finite measure on D with total mass T>0 almost surely and 0<E[T]<infinity. Put U_A=Z(A)/T. Then E[Z(A)]/E[T]-E[U_A]=Cov(T,U_A)/E[T] for each measurable A. Consequently mean normalized measure equals normalized mean measure exactly when Cov(T,U_A)=0 for every A. Independence of total mass and normalized measure is sufficient but unnecessary: three equally likely outcomes T=(1,2,3), U_first=(1,0,1) on two sites give both averages (2/3,1/3), yet T and the normalized measure are dependent. No integrability or independence claim for DGFF extremal mass is inferred from this finite example.

label: proof
statement: For independent bond percolation on the infinite d-regular tree with d>=3, p_c=1/(d-1), theta(p)=0 for p<=p_c, and theta(p)=[2d(d-1)/(d-2)](p-p_c)+O((p-p_c)^2) as p decreases to p_c from above. The positive descendant-survival solution u obeys 1-u=(1-pu)^(d-1); division by u and the implicit-function theorem give the expansion, and theta=1-(1-pu)^d. This is an exact tree analogue, not a high-dimensional lattice solution.

label: proof
statement: On 0<epsilon<1/4, F(epsilon)=epsilon(2+sin(log epsilon)) is strictly increasing, lies between epsilon and 3epsilon, and satisfies log F(epsilon)/log epsilon ->1 as epsilon tends to zero. Nevertheless F(epsilon)/epsilon has no limit. Thus monotonicity plus bounded-ratio beta=1 alone cannot establish asymptotic equivalence to c epsilon. This analytic counterexample is a refuted inference, not a percolation counterexample.

label: source-backed route audit
statement: The C0063-A001 intake attempt displays beta=gamma-Delta with gamma=1 and Delta=2 and claims that this gives beta=1. The displayed arithmetic instead gives -1. This records a route failure in that attempt and does not assert a replacement scaling theorem or equivalence of unresolved amplitude statements. Singular-limit differentiation and a right derivative at criticality still require proof for the requested lattice model.

label: proof
statement: Let G be a finite connected graph with distinct edge weights, T its minimum spanning tree, and G_p its subgraph of edges of weight at most p. For each component C of G_p, the restriction T to C is a spanning tree and the T path between vertices of C stays in C. Therefore max_C diam_intrinsic(C)<=diam(T). A probabilistic lower bound on sublevel intrinsic component diameter transfers directly to the MST; this gives no MST upper bound or high-dimensional cluster estimate by itself.

label: proof
statement: For each n>=3 there is a distinct-weight assignment on K_n such that the MST is a Hamilton path of diameter n-1, while a sublevel including all edges has intrinsic diameter 1. Assign the n-1 path edges the smallest weights and every other edge larger weights. Hence a cluster intrinsic-diameter bound at one threshold does not imply the reverse MST-diameter inequality. This refutes that generic upper-bound route, not torus or hypercube scaling.

label: archival problem context
statement: Historical open-problem target, current status unverified: for an infinite connected bounded-degree graph G satisfying |boundary_E S|>=c|S|^((d-1)/d) for every finite nonempty S, for some c>0 and d>1, must independent bond percolation have p_c(G)<1? The local intake attributes this to the Benjamini-Schramm conjecture in Pete lecture notes, Conjecture 12.7. Positive-Cheeger expansion is a stronger sufficient hypothesis; it does not cover the entire finite-dimensional isoperimetric condition. This goal card fills an exact C0139 anchor absent from the read-only population snapshot and supplies no claimed resolution.

label: proof
statement: Let G be an infinite connected graph of maximum degree D<infinity and edge-Cheeger constant h=inf_(finite nonempty S)|boundary_E S|/|S|>0. For independent bond percolation, 1/(D-1)<=p_c<=1/(1+h)<1. A simple-path first moment proves the lower bound. During cluster exploration after s discoveries and f failures, at least h(s+1)-f boundary edges remain untested. For p>1/(1+h), the comparison walk h+hs-f has positive drift and positive probability to remain positive forever, forcing an infinite cluster. This proves a positive-Cheeger special case; the drift argument does not decide critical equality or the full finite-dimensional isoperimetric conjecture.

label: proof
statement: Every finite nonempty S in the square lattice Z^2 has |boundary_E S|>=4sqrt(|S|), while the edge-Cheeger constant of Z^2 is zero. Indeed, if S occupies a columns and b rows then its edge boundary is at least 2a+2b>=4sqrt(ab)>=4sqrt(|S|); square boxes of side r have boundary/volume=4/r. Thus an IP_2 inequality cannot be substituted for the uniform positive-Cheeger hypothesis in the explicit threshold proof. This does not refute the conjecture that finite isoperimetric dimension greater than one ensures p_c<1.

label: proof
statement: Under the partition convention of Randomstrasse101 Definition 14.2, the shape with one edge uv, U={u} and V={v}, gives a symmetric n by n Rademacher matrix A with zero diagonal. Its expected operator norm is Theta(sqrt(n)), so this shape has exponents f=1/2 and g=0. Deterministically ||A||>=sqrt(n-1) by its Frobenius norm. For each unit real x, P(|x^T A x|>=r)<=2exp(-r^2/4); a 1/4 sphere net of size at most 9^n and integration give the O(sqrt(n)) expectation bound. This does not resolve the existence conjecture for every fixed shape.

label: source-backed scope correction
statement: Definition 14.2 in the cached Randomstrasse101 paper partitions all shape vertices into left and right sets. The diagonal signed-degree construction using the same vertex on both sides and an unindexed leaf requires a broader graph-matrix convention. Its finite norm experiment therefore supplies no special-case answer under this literal definition. The valid one-edge example uses distinct left and right vertices. Exact indexing conventions must be fixed before assigning shape exponents.

label: proof
statement: For any random spanning forest on a countable graph with trivial edge-tail sigma-field, the event that it has infinitely many components has probability zero or one. Finitely many edge changes alter a finite component count by at most finitely much and cannot change finiteness. For every finite edge set K, the infinite-count event can therefore be computed after making all edges in K absent, so it is measurable outside K. In particular FUSF on an infinite connected locally finite network has either infinitely many components almost surely or finitely many almost surely. In the finite case the argument does not make the component count constant.

label: proof
statement: On an infinite connected locally finite network whose underlying graph is a tree and whose edge conductances are positive, the free uniform spanning forest contains every edge almost surely and has exactly one component. Every finite connected induced exhaustion is itself a tree with a unique spanning tree; the free weak limit therefore fixes every edge as present. This is a boundary case of component-count determinism, not an argument for arbitrary networks.
